papers.title_in_file: Quantum algorithms for hypergraph simplex finding
papers.version_note: arXiv:2409.00239v1 [quant-ph], 30 Aug 2024, authors Shalev Ben-David and Zhiying Yu. The text layer is this paper. Mathematics is partly garbled LaTeX: the formulas of Theorem 1, Theorem 19, Lemma 18, Lemma 25 (cost bound) and Table 1 are not cleanly readable, so those results are quoted from the surrounding prose where possible.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper on quantum query complexity of simplex finding in hypergraphs: a rank-reduction reduction from triangle finding, a conversion of nested Johnson-graph quantum walks into adaptive learning graphs, and an O(n^2.455) quantum query algorithm for 4-simplex finding.

existing.value: The paper shows that, for any specific constant rank r, an algorithm for simplex finding in rank-r hypergraphs with n to the power r/2 queries would imply an O(n) algorithm for triangle finding.

assertions.value: The paper states, as a direct consequence of Theorem 1, that a quantum algorithm solving tetrahedron finding with o(n to the power 1.75) queries would give a quantum algorithm solving triangle finding with o(n to the power 1.25) queries.

assertions.reader_inference: Triangle finding has a known O(n^1.25) upper bound, so the corollary links any sub-n^1.75 tetrahedron algorithm to a new triangle record.

assertions.value: The authors describe a randomized reduction that solves the OR of n instances of rank r simplex finding using one simplex finding instance of one higher rank on twice as many vertices, with extra hyperedges from a random complete partite hypergraph so that a simplex using only the second vertex set cannot arise, and they state that the success probability is a constant when r is constant.

assertions.reader_inference: The probability that the r + 1 simplex vertices land in different parts is a constant that depends on r, so the reduction loses a factor that grows with r.

assertions.value: The authors state that the proof of the composition fact used by the reduction uses the negative-weight-adversary characterization of quantum query complexity, so the reduction technically uses the negative-weight adversary method.

assertions.value: The paper cites the result that, for any possibly partial Boolean functions f and g, the quantum query complexity of the composed function is equivalent to the product of the quantum query complexities of f and g, and uses it to say the OR of n copies needs a factor of order the square root of n more queries.
quotes: is equivalent to the product of quantum query complexities of f and g.
since bounded-error quantum query complexity composes multiplicatively
